name: Fireflies
description: A night meadow drawn as a blue screenprint, full of 600 tiny yellow-green fireflies that are dark between flashes, and the beat grid pulls them into unison as strongly as the beat is clear. The meadow is a real 3D place seen through one slowly drifting camera: hatched grass receding to a ragged tree line in three paler layers, bare trees with fine branching, mist in the low distance, light grass stalks and seed heads along the bottom edge. Every pixel is one of six blue inks plus near-black, and tone is the density of fine lines and grain; value is depth, darkest near and palest in the sky above the trees. The fireflies fly in that same space, bigger and brighter near the camera, so near and far ones slide past each other as it drifts. Each firefly runs its own clock and flashes when it runs out; a flash nudges every neighbour a little closer to its own flash, 60 ms late, so flashes relay across the meadow in visible sweeps (Nicky Case's Fireflies model, CC0). On every beat-grid tick (every 1, 2 or 4 beats, whichever puts the flash cycle nearest one second) each clock is pulled toward the tick and retunes its own period (Ermentrout 1991), scaled by the track's beat clarity: a steady beat locks the swarm onto it within about 15 s, while an irregular beat, or one whose clarity is unknown, leaves the swarm free. Every track starts incoherent by design. The world listens only to the slow bass level, averaged over about 4 s: in fuller passages the wind leans the grass and sways the trees harder and the mist drifts faster; it never moves on the beat, which belongs to the fireflies. At near-silence all but 5 % of the fireflies fade out over about 1.5 s, and the meadow stays lit, its wind and mist slower but still moving. Each flash is still a small core with a faint halo (40 ms rise, 0.11 s decay), so a unison flash is hundreds of tiny points rather than a frame-wide lift; the fireflies' glow and the light they cast on the grass and mist come in FF.3. Not certified, and excluded from manual cycling until then.
author: Matt

audio_routes.note: FF.1 — each beatPhase01 wrap is a grid tick; every m-th tick pulls every clock toward 0 by K·0.30 of its wrapped error and retunes its period by K·0.05. K = clamp(2·stems.beatClarity01 − 1, 0, 1), so unknown (0.5) is free (D-257). beatClarity01 and nearSilent01 (the straggler fade) are not declared here: neither is in AudioRoutePrimitives' recordable map, and the committed route_coverage fixtures predate beatClarity01 and never reach near-silence. Both are gated in FirefliesSwarmTests instead.

FF.2 — the world's breath (Matt's "B", D-258 addendum): bassAttRel averaged again over tau = 4 s on the CPU and soft-saturated, 0.5 + 0.5*tanh(4x) (FirefliesWorld.advance). Sets the wind's strength and speed on the grass and the trees and the mist's drift speed, through integrated phases so a change never lurches. Never beat-rate: the beat is the swarm's alone (FA #67).
